**7B.6 Shehbaz Sharif (2024)**  
Overall: **mixed, leaning no**. I found some real tolerance for *reactive* fact-finding and official inquiries, but the broader pattern in 2024 was hostile to independent scrutiny of the government, especially through media pressure, internet blocks, protest restrictions, and weakening of judicial independence.

**Accepted claims**
- **Pakistan to investigate army’s meddling in judiciary, law minister says** | Reuters via Al Jazeera | 2024-03-28 | https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/3/28/pakistan-to-investigate-armys-meddling-in-judiciary-law-minister-says | After six High Court judges alleged ISI intimidation, the Sharif government said it would form an inquiry commission. This is the clearest 2024 positive sign of tolerating an independent-looking investigation into politically sensitive abuse. | QIDs: 7B.6, 7B.2, 7B.1
- **Mohtasib resolves 193,028 complaints, provides relief of Rs 48.98bn** | President of Pakistan | 2024-02-07 | https://president.gov.pk/mohtasib-resolves-193028-complaints-provides-relief-of-rs-4898-billion-2 | The federal ombudsman handled a large volume of complaints and provided relief, showing complaint-handling infrastructure remained active in 2024. This is only weakly connected to Sharif personally, but it does support the existence of an outlet for public grievances. | QIDs: 7B.6
- **PM orders action over ‘ineffective’ track and trace system** | Dawn | 2024-05-08 | https://www.dawn.com/news/1832117 | Sharif ordered action after an inquiry report found the FBR’s track-and-trace system ineffective. This is a concrete example of responding to an internal finding rather than burying it. | QIDs: 7B.6, 7B.5, 7B.3
- **Bisham attack: PM Shehbaz orders immediate action against 5 officials for negligence of duty** | Dawn | 2024-04-06 | https://www.dawn.com/news/1826071/bisham-attack-pm-shehbaz-orders-immediate-action-against-5-officials-for-negligence-of-duty | After an inquiry report on the Bisham attack, Sharif ordered disciplinary action against five officials for negligence. This suggests he sometimes accepted adverse findings and followed them with corrective action. | QIDs: 7B.6
- **PM orders urgent inquiry into Neelum-Jhelum project’s technical fault** | APP | 2024-05-16 | https://www.app.com.pk/national/pm-orders-urgent-inquiry-into-neelum-jhelum-projects-technical-fault/ | Sharif ordered an urgent probe into the Neelum-Jhelum technical fault. That is a genuine fact-finding response, though still reactive and tightly controlled from above. | QIDs: 7B.6, 7B.3
- **Pakistan’s government curbs judiciary’s power after alleged harassment of MPs** | The Guardian | 2024-10-21 | https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/oct/21/pakistans-government-curbs-judiciarys-power-after-alleged-harassment-of-mps | The 26th Amendment weakened judicial independence amid allegations of intimidation and abductions of MPs. That directly cuts against tolerating independent investigation by courts or other neutral institutions. | QIDs: 7B.6, 7B.2
- **Pakistan widening crackdown on dissent** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/pakistan-widening-crackdown-dissent | HRW said the government clamped down on dissenting media, opposition, and NGOs, with pressure that deepened self-censorship and fear. This is strong evidence against tolerating scrutiny of conduct or hidden decisions. | QIDs: 7B.6, 7B.2, 7B.1
- **Social media platform X blocked in Pakistan over national security, ministry says** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-04-17 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/social-media-platform-x-blocked-in-pakistan-over-national-security-ministry-says-3382313 | The state acknowledged blocking X around the election period on national-security grounds, directly restricting criticism, reporting, and monitoring. That is anti-scrutiny behavior, not tolerance of independent investigation. | QIDs: 7B.6, 7B.2, 7B.1
- **Pakistan: New Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act threatens the right to protest** | Amnesty International | 2024-09-09 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/pakistan-the-new-peaceful-assembly-and-public-order-act-threatens-the-right-to-protest/ | Amnesty said the government rushed through a law that criminalized peaceful assembly and expanded restriction powers. This points to repression of scrutiny and civic monitoring rather than openness. | QIDs: 7B.6, 7B.2, 7B.1
- **Dangerous digital crackdown** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-12-12 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/12/dangerous-digital-crackdown | HRW said internet throttling, VPN restrictions, and PECA-based controls were expanding by late 2024. That is evidence of an increasingly controlled information environment, not tolerance for independent investigation. | QIDs: 7B.6, 7B.2, 7B.1

**Search gap**
- I did not find a reliable 2024 source directly documenting transparent handling of Sharif-family assets, campaign finance, hidden conflicts, or a specific corruption investigation he openly permitted.
- The strongest evidence is indirect: a few reactive probes and complaint mechanisms on one side, versus sustained media, protest, and judicial restrictions on the other.
- Because of that, the best-supported reading is **limited tolerance for selected inquiries, but not broad tolerance for independent scrutiny of the ruler or the ruling circle**.
